title: Design a Workflow with Deterministic Checks
subtitle: Advanced · Let evidence control the next step

scenes.title: Map the steps and the gates
scenes.body: The synthetic issue starts with a known defect.
scenes.code:
Issue → review plan → prove failure
Fix → rerun tests → inspect diff → PR
                            ↳ human review
scenes.result: The agent may choose its approach inside scope.
scenes.narration: Put yourself at the moment before a fix is handed off. How do you know it solves the right problem? We will use a fixed regression test and an independent human review. In this order service, the agent can choose how to inspect and edit the validator inside the planned scope. Each transition in the workflow depends on a visible result.
scenes.focus: Two test gates and a human review checkpoint
scenes.action: Mark which evidence controls each transition.

Each transition in the workflow depends

scenes.title: Turn the requirement into observable outcomes
scenes.body: Write the expected result before changing the validator.
scenes.code:
Quantity     1      5      0      -1
Accept?      yes    yes    no     no

Rule: positive integers only.
scenes.result: The expected answers stay fixed across runs.
scenes.narration: Read the issue and write down the expected answer for each example. One and five should be accepted. Zero and negative one should be rejected. Use the zero case for the regression test, and keep the earlier cases in the suite. These fixed inputs give us something concrete to check before and after the edit.
scenes.focus: The zero case is the required regression
scenes.action: Turn the issue into a table of expected results.

scenes.title: Capture the failing case on the original code
scenes.body: An expected failure supplies stronger evidence than an error.
scenes.result:
test_rejects_zero ... FAIL
Assertion: expected False, got True
scenes.narration: Run the suite with the regression in place and the original code still present. Pause at the failure. It's the zero-case assertion, and the validator returned true even though we expected false. An import error would tell a different story. Capture the assertion and its revision. Now we have evidence that the new test actually detects the defect.
scenes.focus: The assertion reveals the exact defect
scenes.action: Run the regression against the original implementation.

scenes.title: Define what happens after the test
scenes.body: Separate the known initial failure from the post-fix gate.
scenes.code:
After the fix:
Test exit code 0 + expected diff → ready for review
Any assertion failure           → inspect and repair
Unexpected files                → inspect scope
scenes.result: Gate evaluation uses the current revision.
scenes.narration: Before asking for the edit, agree on a gate. The post-fix tests must pass, and the files must fit the task. If an assertion fails, inspect it. If the diff includes an unrelated file, follow up before handing it to review. Keep the regression's expected result fixed while trying a repair, so the passing result still answers the original question.
scenes.focus: A failed post-fix test stops the handoff
scenes.action: Set the pass condition before applying the fix.

scenes.title: Run the same test command after the fix
scenes.body: Compare the current run with the observed failure.
scenes.code:
git diff --stat
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
scenes.result:
test_rejects_zero ... ok
Synthetic run: 4 tests pass.
scenes.narration: Run the same command again, this time on the edited revision. The zero-case test now passes, along with the three existing cases. Check the diff and save this output beside the first run. You've just shown a behavior change: the same test observed acceptance before the fix and rejection after it. The reviewer can now evaluate the implementation and scope.

scenes.title: Run independent checks on the PR
scenes.body: Look for a check still pending on the current PR revision.
scenes.result:
Unit tests     pass
Format check   pass
scenes.narration: Once the human author has opened the training pull request, use G H P R checks to see what continuous integration observed. This sample has two completed checks. In your repo, check the required set and what each result belongs to. If a required check is still pending, stay at that gate until it finishes and you can inspect the result.

scenes.action: Inspect the actual check statuses in the approved terminal.

scenes.title: Hand off evidence to the reviewer
scenes.body: GitHub CLI is the authorized review path for this lab.
scenes.code:
Issue #17 · diff · exact test command
Before: zero assertion fails as expected
After: 4 pass · required checks passed
scenes.result: Independent human review via GitHub CLI.
scenes.narration: Now hand over the issue reference, diff, test command, both outputs, and the pull request checks. The reviewer opens the actual change and records their own decision with GitHub CLI. Give them enough to question the result: which assertion failed, what changed, and what was verified. That's the value of a deterministic checkpoint in a workflow that also requires judgment.
scenes.focus: The author hands over evidence, the reviewer decides
scenes.action: Send the issue, diff, and both runs for independent review.
